description.p: Trackhop keeps the same playlist identical on several music services, on a schedule, without rebuilding it by hand. It is the sync engine of the Trackhop Android app as a program for your computer: it runs in the background with an icon next to the clock and keeps running the scheduled syncs while the computer is on.

ul.li: Spotify, YouTube and TIDAL with your own developer key
Navidrome and other Subsonic servers, Jellyfin and Plex
Last.fm, ListenBrainz and SoundCloud links as sources, and CSV, M3U and other playlist files
One-way or two-way syncs, hourly to weekly, with a report of what was added and what was not found
Radio syncs: the songs an internet radio plays, saved to a playlist
Full backups of your playlists, and an API for Home Assistant, scripts and Prometheus

description.p: Its pages open in its own window, and in any browser on this computer at 127.0.0.1, port 8642; nothing outside the computer can reach them. Sign-ins and keys stay on your computer.

screenshot.caption: Syncs with what each run added, removed and did not find
A new sync from one service to another

description.p: Settings with a light or dark look and a notice when a new version is out. The home page shows the last two weeks, the numbers and the latest runs on a wide screen. Syncs writing to the same playlist no longer undo each other. TIDAL is out of beta.
Fewer tracks not found: titles lose credits and remaster notes before the search. Navidrome, Jellyfin, Plex and Last.fm are out of beta.
ListenBrainz works as a target again, Last.fm lists are named as on Last.fm, and a sync with an empty source says so.
When a service sends only part of a playlist, a sync stops before writing instead of adding everything again.
On a server shared by several people, the admin chooses what each one may use. No changes for the desktop app.
The server edition can be shared by several people, each with their own syncs. No changes for the desktop app.
A public NetEase Cloud Music or QQ Music playlist link can be the source of a sync, read-only.
The server's page can be added to a phone's home screen and opens like an app.
The trackhop command: run syncs, read their results and add or remove tracks from a terminal or a script. On Linux, a Flatpak among the release's files.
The Microsoft Store package, with only the official connections.
Finding a radio by name works again when the station directory's usual servers are down.
Shazam syncs: every song you Shazam, in a playlist of your choice on any service.
Radio syncs: the songs an internet radio plays in the hours you choose, saved to a playlist on any service.
Playlists and tracks through the API: create, rename and delete playlists, add and remove tracks.
